correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge3\), the wheel cofactor is \(\det(wI+L(C_m))\), the all-order spectral product yields the exact spoke marginal, and Poisson-kernel averaging reduces \(p_{\mathrm{spoke}}=1/2\) to the claimed scalar polynomial with a unique root in (0,1). Every tree uses m of the 2m edges, so Cauchy–Schwarz is sharp and the constructed law attains \(m/2\) overlap. KL divergence proves its unique entropy maximality among all optimal laws. A monotonic scalar argument and mean-value expansion yield \(3^m(4/3-w_m)\to64/9\); the UST edge probabilities yield the exact overlap excess. The standalone package checker passed 1626 exact/numerical assertions, including enumeration and integer cofactors for \(3\le m\le8\); finite tests are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: On a natural non-edge-transitive infinite graph family, the result explicitly constructs the canonical least-overlapping and highest-entropy sampler from a single algebraic conductance rather than merely asserting a generic convex optimum. The sharp exponentially accurate 4/3 limit supplies stable large-wheel calibration; the exact UST overlap excess proves ordinary uniform sampling is strictly and linearly inefficient. The mathematical need is a fully supported fair random spanning-tree law, and the exact parameter and sharp rate are not immediate from the general minimum-overlap criterion.
